subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For ordinary Claude CLI sessions that are already near or over the native context cap, what should Dashboard `/compact` promise?
rationale: Current source intentionally treats ordinary Claude CLI compaction as backend-owned, and the remaining options affect native transcript access, session rotation, user recovery UX, and compatibility with Claude Code resume behavior.

options.title: Fail Loudly Until Native Recovery Is Proven
options.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned, but make Dashboard and run-loop recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

options.title: Accept Full Native Delegation
options.body: Continue deferring to Claude Code only after maintainers obtain live proof that native compaction preserves resumable context past the cap and can surface a trustworthy status/result to OpenClaw.

options.title: Build OpenClaw Fallback Recovery
options.body: Implement a tested OpenClaw-owned over-cap path that reads the native Claude transcript or uses a fallback model to summarize before any session rotation.

recommendation.title: Fail Loudly Until Native Recovery Is Proven
recommendation.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned, but make Dashboard and run-loop recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the recent Dashboard context UI work and can route the product decision across UI and session-state owners.
